Given that the ray above passes through the point with Cartesian coordinates $(5,3),$ find the polar equation of the ray. Assume that the polar angle is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$

$\theta =$ 
$\operatorname{arctan}⁡($ {{field-1}} 
$).$
worked_solution:
The angle that the ray makes with the positive $x$-axis is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{3}{5}).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since the ray lies in the first quadrant, the polar equation is  

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\,\frac{3}{5}\,).
$$
